newsitem.title: GREECE: GENERAL NEWS DIGEST - GREECE - OCT 10.
newsitem.headline: GENERAL NEWS DIGEST - GREECE - OCT 10.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek press:

--With the presentation today in Parliament of the new government's policy statements, Prime Minister Costas Simitis will outline the austere economic policy to be followed next year, pointing to the need for Greece to make up the distance separating itself from its European Union partners. But he will confine himself to general statements as there is still disagreement within the government as to where the revenues will come from.

--Greek-Turkish relations are back in the spotlight, following the crash of a Turkish F-16 in the eastern Aegean on Tuesday as joint Greek-Cypriot military exercises ended. 'No dialogue' with Turkey, says Athens, with Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos saying there was no pressure from any quarter for one.

--Defeated New Democracy leadership candidate George Souflias rebuffs ND president Miltiades Evert's overtures for inclusion in his hand-picked political advisory body. Souflias says the recent re-election of Evert as party leader indicates a "transitional period" and that a forthcoming party congress will have the final say on who will be leader.
--Definitely at a distance: Evert and Souflias agree to disagree on everything as the distance between them grows a little yesterday. The crisis in ND intensifies.
--6.4 Richter quake rattles Cyprus but seismologists are more concerned about the recent 5.1 tremor in Pylos, Greece.

--Bound for the gallows. An Alexandroupolis court decision to return three Turkish soldiers to Ankara, following their dramatic escape to Greece on Monday, has drawn fire from politicians and Amnesty International, which "fears for their fate".
--Banking the most lucrative and respected profession, new poll reveals. Tax collectors fail to shake off their centuries-old bad image.
--Wage-earners and pensioners get flayed. Finance ministry figures show an 8.0 percent increase in incomes but a 28 percent increase in taxes.
--Recent high court decision that transferring local height regulations on buildings to other areas is illegal leaves thousands of construction projects 'in the air'.
--No surprises in yesterday's election of Parliament deputy speakers. Everyone voted according to form, banishing memories of Monday's mutiny in ruling party PASOK and ND.

--Government's plans to abolish tax exemptions for life and health insurance policies brings four million policy-holders face to face with the prospect of paying more tax. The plans have caused unrest in the insurance market.
